recommendations.title: 861/862 vs 858/859 (FVG tolerance 9p vs 15p) -- real data currently running AGAINST the backtest, sample too thin to mean anything yet
recommendations.detail: Checked 2026-10-03, real trades since attach (2026-09-30): 861 (9p) net -168.1p/n=14 vs control 858 (15p) net +10.1p/n=24; 862 (9p trail8) net -305.8p/n=14 vs control 859 (15p trail8) net -86.5p/n=24 -- opposite direction from the backtest, which favored 9p on every axis (avg +12.92p vs +5.21p, WR 69.9% vs 65.6%, DD 5.56% vs 7.30%, real $10k basis, n=1213 real signals). Dug into why: 861 is a strict subset of 858's trades (same 7 signals, byte-identical entry/exit prices on every shared one -- confirmed no implementation bug, no FVG-selection difference). The tighter tolerance simply excluded 5 signals 858 caught, and 4 of those 5 were real winners (+30.0p, +56.5p, +53.8p, +52.8p) with only 1 small loser (-14.9p) -- that's the entire gap. This is ordinary small-sample variance (12-14 real trades vs the 1213-signal backtest population), not evidence the backtest is wrong or the fork is broken. DO NOT retire 858/859 or draw any conclusion from this -- needs meaningfully more real trades (same order of magnitude as the original validation) before the real data says anything trustworthy either way.

recommendations.title: 860 vs 808 (trail-past-target@5p) -- 860's own mechanism has had ZERO real chances to activate yet, not just a thin sample
recommendations.detail: Checked 2026-10-03. TC trades rarely -- only 4 real signals total since July (09-11, 09-23, 09-28, 10-01). 860 wasn't attached until 09-29, so it could only ever see the last 1-2 of those; it caught exactly one (2026-10-01, entry 4152.66). That trade hit its stop-loss directly ([sl 4160.92], -83.2p) without ever reaching the point where trail-past-target would arm -- 808 (control) shows the IDENTICAL entry/exit/loss on the same real trade, because both forks are just reporting the same plain stop-out; the mechanism 860 exists to test never got a chance to engage at all. This is not 'too thin to tell' in the usual noisy-small-sample sense -- it's zero real evidence either way, because the one trade available couldn't have differentiated the two designs regardless of outcome. No action -- just keep waiting for TC's next real signal, and specifically one that reaches its TP1-equivalent arm point, before this comparison means anything.
